column4: Description

HR received a monthly door-access movement report from the access-control system: one row per employee per day, with alternating *In* and *Out*
swipe columns. Turning it into office hours by hand was slow and error-prone. This epic delivers a command-line Python script (pandas + openpyxl)
that reads the report, pairs each check-in with a valid checkout, adds shift and email details from a roster, assigns night-shift visits to the
correct work date, and writes an Excel workbook with an Attendance sheet and an Audit Log sheet.
Scope: movement report (CSV or XLSX), optional previous-month report, optional roster, Excel output, console use only.
Out of scope: compliance policy, users, database and web interface.

Benefit:
- Replaces manual matching with a repeatable process that gives the same output for the same input.
- Nothing is silently dropped: every skipped, blank or unresolved item is explained in the Audit Log.
- Defines the business rules that the web engine (ATT-E2) later reuses.
- Prefers a blank to a guess, which makes the report safer for payroll, audit and operations use.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A monthly report produces one workbook containing an Attendance sheet and an Audit Log sheet.
2. Every check-in is either paired with a checkout, or kept with a blank checkout and logged.
3. Every checkout that cannot be used is logged as an orphan and excluded from Attendance.
4. Night-shift visits are reported on the day the shift started.
5. Visits that started in the previous month are not counted in the current month's totals.
6. The README lets a new developer find where each rule lives and which tests to run.

As an HR analyst, I want to give the script the raw movement report as CSV or Excel, so that I don't have to clean the export first.
The script accepts `.csv` and `.xlsx`. The real header row is the row where a column equals `empcode` (case-insensitive), searched in the first 15 rows
(`HEADER_PROBE`, `MAX_HEADER_SCAN_ROWS`); anything above it is discarded. If no such row exists, the run stops with a clear error naming the missing
header instead of treating a title row as data.
Done when: a report with three title rows above the table loads from the `EmpCode` row; a file without `EmpCode` stops with a readable error.

Arch Review: No

As an HR analyst, I want each employee's swipes normalised and grouped, so that one person is never split into two.
Employee IDs are normalised (`"158920"`, `158920.0` and `" 158920 "` all become `158920`). Each row's date and time are combined into one timestamp;
unreadable values are skipped and logged. Every employee gets a sorted list of check-ins and a sorted list of checkouts, with duplicate timestamps removed.
Done when: the same ID in two formats gives one employee; two identical swipe times give one event.

Arch Review: No

As an HR analyst, I want every check-in matched to the right checkout, so that hours in the office are correct.
A check-in takes the earliest unused checkout that is later than it, before the employee's next check-in, on the same or the next calendar day, and within
`MAX_SHIFT_HOURS` (18). A checkout is used once. The rules are strict on purpose: no match is better than a wrong match.
Done when: 16:10 to 18:11 the same day gives one visit of 2.02 hours; a checkout 19 hours later is not paired; two check-ins before one checkout leave
the checkout for the second.

Arch Review: Yes. The pairing rules decide every result. Changing `MAX_SHIFT_HOURS` or `_find_checkout()` can create false matches across days.

column3: ATT-1.4 Handle missing and orphan swipes
column4:
As an HR analyst, I want unmatched swipes kept visible, so that I can follow up instead of losing data.
A check-in with no valid checkout stays in Attendance with a blank checkout and blank hours, and an audit entry *No matching checkout*. A checkout that no
check-in can use is excluded from Attendance and logged as *Orphan checkout*. No hours are ever invented.
Done when: a lone check-in appears with blank hours plus an audit entry; a leading checkout appears only in the Audit Log.

Arch Review: Yes. Audit completeness and the "leave blank, never guess" policy.

column3: ATT-1.5 Enrich with the shift roster
column4:
As an HR analyst, I want name, email and shift added to each visit, so that the report can be filtered and shared.
An optional roster (Excel) is read into stable `ShiftRecord` entries keyed by employee ID. Each matching visit gets email and shift timing. An employee who
is not in the roster is still reported, with blank roster fields and an audit entry.
Done when: matching visits show email and shift; an unknown ID produces an audit entry naming it.

Arch Review: No

As an HR analyst, I want night-shift visits reported on the day the shift started, so that one shift is not split over two dates.
For an overnight roster shift such as `4:00 PM - 1:30 AM`, a check-in after midnight and before the shift end belongs to the previous work date. Day
shifts and later check-ins keep their own date. Only the reporting date changes; the stored check-in timestamp does not.
Done when: for `4:00 PM - 1:30 AM`, a check-in at `2026-08-04 00:52` is reported on `2026-08-03` and one at `2026-08-04 15:42` on `2026-08-04`.

Arch Review: Yes. The work date drives daily totals and merging; the shift end is the cut-off and must be parsed reliably.

As an HR analyst, I want the last day of the previous month considered, so that a check-in on the last evening can pair with the checkout
on the first morning.
With an optional previous-month report, only its final transaction date is loaded and its events are placed before the current events. They are used for
pairing only; visits whose check-in is in the previous month are excluded from the current month's output and totals.
Done when: a 31 July 22:00 check-in pairs with a 1 August 06:00 checkout, and that visit is not counted in August.

Arch Review: Yes. Month ownership of hours and the risk of double counting.

As an HR analyst, I want an estimated checkout for an overnight shift on the last day, so that the final night shift isn't left blank.
The fallback applies only when the check-in is on the latest transaction date, the checkout is missing, the roster shift parses, and the shift crosses
midnight. The next day's roster shift end is used (31 August, `4:30 PM - 1:30 AM` gives 1 September 01:30). Day shifts and earlier dates are never
estimated. The value is an estimate, not a real swipe.
Done when: the example above gives 1 Sep 01:30; a day-shift employee keeps a blank checkout.

Arch Review: Yes. Policy on estimated data. The web engine chose a different rule (see the comparison at the end).

As an HR analyst, I want hours per visit and a total per day, so that I can see time spent in the office.
Visit hours are checkout minus check-in, rounded to 2 decimals. Visits are grouped by employee and work date. The daily total is written on the group's
first row, later rows stay blank, and the Date and Daily Total cells are merged vertically in Excel. Every visit row is kept.
Done when: visits of 2.02 and 3.50 hours on one date give a daily total of 5.52 on the first row.

Arch Review: No

column3: ATT-1.10 Excel report and audit log
column4:
As an HR analyst, I want one workbook with attendance and issues, so that I can review and share the result.
The Attendance sheet has: name, employee ID, email, shift, year, month, week, checked-in date, checked-out date, hours, date, daily total. The Audit Log
sheet has: employee ID, name, issue, details, timestamp. Headers and date columns are styled (`openpyxl`).
Done when: the file has both sheets and the column order matches `OUTPUT_COLUMNS` and `AUDIT_COLUMNS`.

Arch Review: No

As an HR analyst, I want to run the script and answer prompts, so that I don't edit code for each month.
`python3 attendance_engine.py` asks for the current report (required), the previous report (optional), the roster (optional) and the output name, with a
default name built from the data.
Done when: running with only the required file still produces a workbook, with no roster fields.

Arch Review: No

As a developer, I want a README with the mental model and change points, so that I can change a rule safely.
It covers the runtime order, the five key methods, the rules that decide the result, safe customisation points, risky changes and a test checklist
(same-day, overnight, missing checkout, orphan checkout, month boundary, final-date fallback, employee not in roster).
Done when: a new developer can locate where to change a rule and which cases to test.

Arch Review: No

The version-1 logic is rewritten in TypeScript as a pure module of the Express backend (`backend/src/engine`, no database access) and extended with the
company attendance policy: a day counts at 7.0 hours, a week needs 3 office days including every working Wednesday, and a month needs an average of
7.0 hours per working day. A processing service loads the stored data, runs the engine, and saves attendance rows, audit issues and Wednesday records in
one transaction. Results are checked against the Python script for July and August (golden tests).
Scope: pairing, work-day assignment, hours, eligibility, compliance, audit issues, month processing.
Out of scope: screens (ATT-E3 to ATT-E5), manual edits and authentication.

Benefit:
- The same policy is applied the same way to every employee, with no manual calculation.
- Same numbers as the script, proven by golden tests, so the move from script to web did not change results.
- A pure module is easy to test and safe to change.
- Every data problem is recorded, so results can be explained.

Acceptance criteria:
1. July and August outputs match the Python results.
2. Compliance follows [policies.md](policies.md) exactly (7.0 hours, 3 days a week, every working Wednesday, monthly average).
3. Reprocessing a month never loses manual adjustments, overrides, holidays or leaves.
4. Every data problem becomes an audit issue.
5. A failed processing run leaves the previous results unchanged.

As HR, I want swipes paired into visits automatically, so that office hours can be calculated without manual matching.
Per employee, in time order: a checkout on the same or next day, up to 20 hours after a check-in, pairs with it. A check-in followed by another check-in
becomes an open visit with no hours (*Missing checkout*). A checkout with no check-in, or one that is too late, is ignored (*Orphan checkout*). A check-in
still pending at the end of the data becomes an open visit.
Done when: 22:00 with a 05:00 checkout the next day gives one visit; a 21-hour gap gives no pair and two audit issues.

Arch Review: Yes. State machine design and the 20-hour limit (the script used 18); pure function with typed input and output.

column3: ATT-2.2 Assign each visit to a work day
column4:
As HR, I want each visit assigned to the correct work date, so that night shifts count once.
Normal shifts use the check-in date. For overnight shifts, a check-in after midnight up to shift end + 60 minutes belongs to the previous day. With no shift
on file, an employee with more evening (17:00 or later) than morning (06:00 to 11:59) check-ins is treated as 18:00 to 06:00 and logged *Inferred overnight
pattern*. Visits sharing a work date form one day group.
Done when: with a `4:00 PM - 1:30 AM` shift, a 02:15 check-in belongs to the previous day (inside the 60-minute buffer).

Arch Review: Yes. Buffer value, inference heuristic, and handling of clock times as UTC (no time-zone shifts).

As HR, I want hours calculated exactly as the script did, so that totals match.
Visit hours are rounded to 2 decimals with ties to even, matching Python (JavaScript `Math.round` differs). The daily total is the sum of closed visits, and
empty if none are closed. A day with a closed and an open visit shows the total but is flagged *Daily total is partial*. The month total sums the daily
totals, treating empty as 0.
Done when: rounding results equal Python's `round` on a set of known values.

Arch Review: Yes. Rounding parity and the meaning of empty versus zero.

As HR, I want month edges handled safely, so that hours are never double counted or lost.
The previous month's last day of swipes is loaded for pairing only, and visits that started in the previous month are dropped. A visit on the last day of
the month is skipped and logged *Skipped - month boundary*, because its checkout may be in next month's file that isn't available yet.
Done when: a last-day visit has no hours and one audit issue; a night shift from the last day of the previous month pairs but is not counted.

Arch Review: Yes. A policy trade-off (see ATT-1.8) and a candidate for later change once next month's data exists.

As HR, I want shift, department, manager and email read from the roster, so that rules and views use correct data.
The override shift wins over the base shift. Shift text such as `9:00 AM - 6:30 PM` (separators `to`, `-`, `–`) is parsed, with `12:xx AM` as hour 0 and
`12:xx PM` as hour 12; unreadable text means no shift. Manager email is not in the roster, so it is resolved by matching the manager's name to another
employee; unresolved names are listed in one audit issue.
Done when: `12:30 AM - 9:00 AM` starts at hour 0; an unknown manager name leaves the email blank and appears in one issue.

Arch Review: No

As a policy owner, I want exempt shifts excluded from the policy, so that it applies only to the right people.
Employees on exactly the general shift `9:00 AM - 6:30 PM` are exempt and get `NA` for daily, weekly and monthly compliance. Every other shift, and
employees with no shift, are evaluated.
Done when: a general-shift employee has `NA` in all three compliance values.

Arch Review: Yes. Treating an unknown shift as eligible is a policy choice that should be confirmed with the owner.

column3: ATT-2.7 Daily, weekly and monthly compliance
column4:
As HR, I want Yes / No / NA flags at three levels, so that I can see who meets the policy.
Daily: `NA` if not eligible or no total, `No` below 7.0 hours, `Yes` at 7.0 or more. Weekly, using fixed 7-day blocks (1-7, 8-14, 15-21, 22-28, 29-end):
`Yes` only if every working Wednesday is attended with 7+ hours and attended days are at least `min(3, working weekdays)`; holiday Wednesdays are not
required; leaves do not change it. Monthly: `Yes` only if hours divided by working days is at least 7.0 (working days = weekdays minus holidays minus the
employee's leaves; zero gives `No`) and every evaluated week is `Yes`.
Done when: three 7+ hour days with a 6.5-hour Wednesday give a `No` week; a short last block of two weekdays needs only two attended days.

Arch Review: Yes. Fixed blocks instead of calendar weeks, one source for constants, behaviour with holidays and leaves.

As HR, I want every data problem recorded, so that nothing is dropped silently.
Seven issue types are saved per month: missing checkout, orphan checkout, partial daily total, month boundary, inferred overnight pattern, no roster
match, and manager email unresolved. An employee who is not in the roster still gets attendance rows (name from the swipe file, manager `NA`, eligible).
Done when: swipes for an unknown ID produce rows and a *No roster match* issue.

Arch Review: No

As HR, I want one action to process a month, so that results update from the latest data.
`POST /api/months/:ym/process` loads swipes, roster, holidays, leaves, fallback names and the previous month's last day, then runs the engine. In one
transaction it deletes and re-inserts the month's attendance rows, audit issues and Wednesday rows and refreshes transport opt-in. Adjustments,
overrides, holidays and leaves are kept. It returns 400 for a bad month and 404 if the movement file or roster is missing.
Done when: an adjustment still applies after reprocessing; a mid-run failure leaves the old results in place.

Arch Review: Yes. Transaction boundary, synchronous processing (may need a job queue at larger sizes), chunked inserts.

As a developer, I want golden tests against the Python output, so that a rule change cannot slip in unnoticed.
Stored July and August expectations from the script are compared with the engine output. A deliberate rule change must update the golden files and
[policies.md](policies.md) together.
Done when: the golden suite passes in CI and fails if a constant such as the 7.0-hour threshold is changed.

Arch Review: Yes. Fixture strategy and the process for changing a rule.

column3: ATT-E3 Upload and Data Management Dashboard
column4:
The `/upload` page where HR loads and maintains everything the engine needs: roster, monthly movement file, optional transport list, public holidays and
employee leaves. It has a card per file kind with validation, blank templates, a months list with status, upload history, a holiday calendar and a leave
calendar, plus actions to process or delete a month.
Scope: uploads, validation, templates, months, holidays, leaves, history. Out of scope: showing results (ATT-E4).

Benefit:
- HR prepares data without developer help.
- Bad files are rejected with a clear reason before they can affect results.
- A month can be re-run safely when inputs change.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Only `.csv` and `.xlsx` files are accepted, and each kind is validated.
2. A failed upload changes nothing.
3. The latest roster and transport files replace the old ones; a movement file replaces only its own month.
4. The selected month is shared by all pages.
5. Holidays and leaves can be maintained, and the page states when a reprocess is needed.

column3: ATT-3.1 Upload roster, movement and transport files
column4:
As HR, I want to upload each file type, so that a month can be processed.
`POST /api/uploads` takes the kind and a file. A roster or transport upload replaces the existing one. A movement upload replaces only the month it
belongs to (the month with the most swipes). A roster upload also rebuilds manager users (ATT-6.4). Everything runs in one database transaction, and
swipe inserts are chunked for large files.
Done when: a second movement upload for the same month leaves only the newer swipes; a corrupt file leaves the previous data untouched.

Arch Review: Yes. Replace semantics, transaction scope and large-file insert limits.

As HR, I want clear errors for a wrong file, so that I can fix it quickly.
A wrong file type, missing header, no employees, no swipes or a bad date each returns a 400 with a specific message; date errors name the row number.
Nothing is saved on error.
Done when: a leaves file with a bad date on row 7 shows a message naming row 7.

Arch Review: No

As HR, I want a template for each file kind, so that I prepare data in the right format.
`GET /api/templates/:kind` returns an `.xlsx` with the expected headers; each upload card has a download button.
Done when: an unmodified template with data filled in uploads without errors.

Arch Review: No

As HR, I want to see each month's status, so that I know what is ready.
`GET /api/months` lists months with status (uploaded, processed). The selected month is kept in the URL and passed to every page.
Done when: picking a month on one page opens the same month on the others.

Arch Review: No

column3: ATT-3.5 Process or delete a month
column4:
As HR, I want to run or remove a month, so that I control the results.
Process runs the engine (ATT-2.9). Delete removes the month's processed data and uploads and asks for confirmation first.
Done when: confirming Delete removes the month; cancelling changes nothing.

Arch Review: No

As HR, I want to see past uploads, so that I can trace what was loaded and when.
`GET /api/uploads` returns the kind, file name and time of each upload, shown newest first.
Done when: a new upload appears in the list immediately.

Arch Review: No

As HR, I want to set holidays for a month, so that policy is relaxed on those days.
`GET` and `PUT /api/months/:ym/holidays` (PUT replaces the month's set). Holidays reduce working days and relax the weekly requirement. A note tells HR that
the month must be reprocessed for compliance values to change.
Done when: after reprocessing, a holiday Wednesday is no longer required.

Arch Review: No

As HR, I want to record employee leaves, so that working-day counts are fair.
HR can search an employee and add, remove or replace their leave days on a calendar, or upload a leaves file (header aliases such as `emplid`, `empcode`,
`date`; Excel or ISO dates). Leaves affect only the monthly ratio, not the weekly requirement.
Done when: two leave days reduce that employee's working days by two after reprocessing.

Arch Review: No

As HR, I want transport opt-in to show without reprocessing, so that changes appear at once.
After a transport upload, `refreshTransportOptIn` updates the saved attendance rows of processed months. The flag is display data only and does not
affect compliance.
Done when: uploading a transport file updates the dashboard flag for an already processed month.

Arch Review: Yes. A write path outside the normal processing transaction.

The `/dashboard` and `/audit` pages. After a month is processed, HR and managers review it through summary cards and filters and four tabs (Employee,
Manager, Ledger, Directory). HR can correct a day's hours when swipes are wrong, review all data issues on the Audit Log page, and export the month to
Excel.
Scope: viewing, filters, adjustments, audit page, export. Out of scope: restricting a manager to their own team (backlog).

Benefit:
- Answers "who is compliant, and why?" within seconds.
- Manual corrections are visible, reversible and never overwrite engine results.
- The Excel export lets results be shared and archived.

Acceptance criteria:
1. The dashboard and the export show the same rows, with adjustments applied.
2. Filters work on monthly compliance, week, weekly compliance and transport.
3. Manual changes are marked (`add`, `edit`, `delete`) and can be undone.
4. Every page has loading, empty and error states.
5. Downloads work while signed in.

As HR, I want totals and filters, so that I can narrow down to what matters.
Cards show total employees, daily hours entries, total work hours logged and check-in sessions. Filters cover monthly compliance, week, weekly
compliance and transport opt-in. Data comes from `GET /api/months/:ym/attendance`.
Done when: applying a filter updates the cards and every tab.

Arch Review: No

As a viewer, I want one employee's days and flags, so that I can explain their result.
Shows each day's visits, daily total and compliance flag, with open visits and adjusted rows clearly marked, plus the employee's weekly and monthly
compliance.
Done when: an open visit is shown with no hours and a visible marker.

Arch Review: No

As a manager, I want my team's hours and compliance, so that I can follow up.
Rows are grouped by manager email from the roster, with counts and totals and a jump to an employee. Currently every signed-in user can see every manager
(see backlog).
Done when: the team total equals the sum of the team's rows.

Arch Review: No

As HR, I want every row in one searchable table, so that I can check details.
Shows all visit rows of the month with search; pagination or a virtual list is added if volume grows.
Done when: the row count equals the Excel export.

Arch Review: No

As HR, I want an employee directory, so that I can see department, shift, manager and transport opt-in in one place.
Lists employees with a link to their detail; employees not in the roster appear with an *Unassigned* shift.
Done when: an employee missing from the roster is listed as Unassigned.

Arch Review: No

As HR, I want to add, edit or delete a day's hours, so that missed swipes and approved corrections are reflected.
`PUT /api/months/:ym/hours` accepts hours (0 to 24) for a date in the month; one adjustment per employee per day. The action is derived: engine rows exist
gives `edit` or `delete`; no rows but the employee has others that month gives `add`; no rows at all gives 404. Adjustments are stored separately and
applied on read, so engine output is never overwritten. The daily total and daily flag are recomputed; weekly and monthly flags are not. An `add` is
ignored if swipes later appear for that date. `DELETE /api/months/:ym/hours/:employeeId/:date` restores the engine value.
Done when: editing to 7.5 hours gives a `Yes` daily flag and an `edit` marker; undoing restores the engine value.

Arch Review: Yes. Separation from engine data, the known mismatch between daily and weekly/monthly flags, and the missing audit trail.

As HR, I want to see and filter all issues, so that I can find the cause of an unexpected number.
`GET /api/months/:ym/audit` lists the issues, filterable by type and searchable by employee name or ID.
Done when: filtering by *Missing checkout* shows only those issues.

Arch Review: No

As HR, I want to download the month as Excel, so that I can share or archive it.
`GET /api/months/:ym/export.xlsx` builds the workbook with ExcelJS from the same rows as the dashboard, including adjustments. The browser uses
`downloadFile` (a fetch with the Bearer token saved through a temporary object URL), because a plain link cannot send the Authorization header.
Done when: a signed-in user downloads a file with the month in its name; an expired token sends the user to sign in.

Arch Review: Yes. The authenticated download pattern, and in-memory building that may need streaming for very large months.

column3: ATT-4.9 Loading, empty and error states
column4:
As a user, I want clear page states, so that I know whether data is loading, missing or failed.
A shared `useAsync` hook and common components show a spinner, an empty message or an error with a retry on every page.
Done when: a failed call shows an error message and a retry action.

Arch Review: No

The `/wednesday` page supports the policy that everyone should be in the office on Wednesdays. When a month is processed, one record per employee per
Wednesday is saved. The page shows an employee-by-Wednesday matrix, turnout against the 75% target, attendance tiers and summary statistics, and lets HR
override a single entry.
Scope: matrix, statistics, tiers, overrides, holiday handling. Out of scope: the weekly 7-hour rule (ATT-2.7).

Benefit:
- Leadership can see turnout on the policy's key day and whether the 75% target is met.
- HR can record exceptions without changing swipe data.
- Holiday Wednesdays do not distort the figures.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Every employee in the roster has a record for every Wednesday of the month.
2. Turnout, headcount, peak and lowest dates, tiers and distribution follow [policies.md](policies.md) section 9.
3. Overrides can be set, changed and cleared, and survive reprocessing.
4. Holiday Wednesdays are excluded from all figures.

As HR, I want each employee against each Wednesday, so that I can see attendance at a glance.
Attended means the employee has a work day on that date, with any hours, including an open visit; this is separate from the 7-hour rule. Everyone in the
roster gets a row, including people with no swipes. Data comes from `GET /api/months/:ym/wednesday`.
Done when: a 3-hour visit on a Wednesday shows as attended.

Arch Review: No

As leadership, I want turnout against the 75% target, so that I can see whether the policy is working.
Shows turnout per Wednesday, headcount per date, and the peak and lowest dates (the first one on a tie).
Done when: 60 of 80 staff attending shows 75% turnout and the target as met.

Arch Review: No

As leadership, I want employees grouped by Wednesday attendance, so that I can see the spread.
Tiers: Perfect (all working Wednesdays), High (75% or more), Moderate (50% or more), Low (above 0 and under 50%), Zero. Also shows average days attended,
total footfall and the distribution of days.
Done when: 3 of 4 Wednesdays places an employee in High.

Arch Review: No

As HR, I want to mark one person present or absent for a Wednesday, so that exceptions are recorded.
`PUT /api/months/:ym/wednesday` with `{employeeId, wednesday, attended}`; `null` removes the override. Overrides are stored in a separate table, apart from
engine data, and survive reprocessing.
Done when: an override still applies after the month is reprocessed.

Arch Review: Yes. Separation from engine data, precedence rules and the missing audit trail.

As HR, I want holiday Wednesdays excluded, so that nobody is penalised for them.
Holiday Wednesdays are not required and not counted. Holidays are read live, so a holiday edit shows on this page without reprocessing, unlike the
weekly and monthly compliance values.
Done when: marking a Wednesday as a holiday removes it from the target figures immediately.

Arch Review: Yes. Live reads versus stored results, and the temporary inconsistency with the weekly rule until reprocessing.

As leadership, I want an estimate of office hours, so that summaries show effort as well as headcount.
Each attended Wednesday is credited as an estimated 8.0 in-office hours (`HOURS_PER_DAY`) in the summary figures.
Done when: three attended Wednesdays show 24 estimated hours.

Arch Review: No

column3: ATT-E6 Access Control and Okta Sign-in
column4:
Sign-in and authorisation for the whole application. Authentication uses Okta (OIDC Authorization Code with PKCE). Authorisation is separate: an Okta user
can enter only if listed in the `app_users` table as superadmin, HR or manager. Managers are created from each roster upload, HR users are added by the
superadmin on the Access page, and the superadmin is a database row. Every API call except `/api/health` is verified.
Scope: sign-in, token verification, roles, Access page, sign-out, demo mode, go-live checklist. Out of scope: restricting data by manager (backlog).

Benefit:
- Company single sign-on and MFA, with no separate passwords to manage.
- Access changes take effect on the next request.
- Manager access follows the roster automatically, so it needs no second list.
- The application can still run locally without Okta.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A signed-out user is redirected to Okta and returned to the requested page.
2. A signed-in user not in `app_users` sees an Access denied screen (403); a missing or invalid token gets 401.
3. Roles are enforced: only the superadmin can use `/api/admin`.
4. Each roster upload rebuilds the manager users without touching HR or superadmin rows.
5. Signing out ends both the app session and the Okta session.
6. With Okta unset the app runs in demo mode; placeholder values stop the app from starting.
7. The go-live checklist has passed against a real Okta tenant (open item).

As a user, I want to sign in through Okta, so that I use my company login.
`AuthGate` handles `/login/callback`, redirects signed-out users to Okta with a PKCE challenge, and returns them to the page they asked for. Tokens are
kept in `sessionStorage` and renewed automatically; if silent renewal is blocked, a 401 triggers a fresh login (at most once a minute).
Done when: a signed-out user opening `/dashboard` lands on `/dashboard` after signing in.

Arch Review: Yes. PKCE flow, token storage in `sessionStorage` (XSS trade-off) and renewal behaviour.

column3: ATT-6.2 Access denied and sign-in failed screens
column4:
As a user, I want a clear message when I can't get in, so that I know what to do next.
A 403 shows Access denied with the refused email and an option to switch account. A 401 or other failure shows Sign-in failed with a retry.

As a security owner, I want every API call verified, so that only authorised users get data.

Identifiers are `preferred_username`, `email` and `sub` when it contains `@`, or the single claim set in `OKTA_IDENTITY_CLAIM`. The user is looked up with
